solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Capital city, where a country bumpkin's heading back

indicators.note: back tells us the string built from the following pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: Togo is a West African country

indicators.note: a bumpkin's heading is the letter at the front of that word

explanation.surface: A rustic visitor heads home from a big South American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole string A + TOGO + B (from 'heading' of bumpkin's).
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia.

clue.text: Hostile reaction when champion goes on strike

indicators.note: goes on signals one piece placed after the other in a run

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
to lash is to strike with a whip

explanation.surface: Fans turn hostile when their hero walks out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong adverse public response to some change.

clue.text: Biscuit again unwrapped, slightly dirty inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other
unwrapped means the outer letters of again are peeled off

parts.note: ribald humour is mildly coarse or risqué

explanation.surface: A biscuit unwrapped a second time turns out a bit grubby within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapped' strips A and N from 'again' to leave GAI, which holds RIBALD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garibaldi is a British currant-filled biscuit named after the Italian general.

clue.text: Seat launched, it's said?

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: something launched is thrown, as a javelin

explanation.surface: A query whether a seat was hurled into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is the ceremonial chair of a monarch.

clue.text: Promise to bind joint with last of elastic, fibres twisted together

indicators.note: to bind means to wrap round, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
the hip is a joint of the body

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of elastic

explanation.surface: Instructions for strapping a sore joint with elastic bandage and twisted fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipcord is a tightly twisted cord, and also a strong ribbed worsted cloth.

clue.text: Ludicrously complex alliance of former British and Irish premiers

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74
Mary Robinson was President of Ireland, here loosely called a premier

explanation.surface: A cross-border coalition of past national leaders, which sounds absurdly complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famous for drawing absurdly elaborate contraptions; his name became the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraption described this way is absurdly over-engineered for a simple task.

clue.text: Account behind the bar reserved by staff for drinking

indicators.note: reserved by means held in by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a staff is a pole or rod
a pub tab is a running account kept by the bar

explanation.surface: A bar tab kept aside by the employees for their own drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is safe to drink, so the word means fit for drinking.

clue.text: Beef, yours truly said, for Daisy

parts.note: an ox is a beef animal

indicators.note: said marks a word spoken and heard as another

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, I

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that beef is meant for a woman named Daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye is a wild daisy with large white flowers.

clue.text: Stop in scruffy side street

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy, so the letters of side are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone comes to a halt in a shabby little back road.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease doing something.

clue.text: Losing head, person frightening nurse, say?

indicators.note: losing head means the front letter is dropped

parts.note: someone who frightens is a scarer

explanation.surface: A horror figure loses their head and turns out to be a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is one example of someone who looks after others, hence 'say?'.

clue.text: Cold as a deck when quarter scrubbed?

definitions.text: as a deck when quarter scrubbed?
definitions.meaning: a pack missing one of its four suits, the red one shown as ♥, lacks that suit

explanation.surface: A card deck missing a quarter of itself would be oddly heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: A deck has four suits, so a quarter scrubbed is one whole suit gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitiless person is described as unfeeling, lacking warmth or compassion.

clue.text: Look precarious, as did Damocles' sword?

definitions.meaning: to be in a very unstable or risky state
the sword over Damocles was held by a single horsehair

explanation.surface: Something looks precarious, like the sword over Damocles.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation where survival depends on the slightest support.

clue.text: A noble sort of northern country

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters of a noble rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A nobleman of a northern country, of a sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a country on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Book chap formulates

parts.note: a chap is a he
to brew a plan is to formulate it

explanation.surface: A man devises a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrews is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Individual muscle cut back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in the opposite direction
cut means a letter is removed from the word's tail

parts.note: flesh is muscle and soft tissue

explanation.surface: A particular muscle is cut back, as a surgeon or butcher might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops H from FLESH, and 'back' turns FLES around.
explanation.definitionFit: One's self is one's individual identity.

clue.text: Black fish in hotel, skinned, well past sell-by date?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
skinned means the outer letters of hotel are stripped off

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Blackened fish served in a hotel, skinned but well past its sell-by date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' reduces hotel to OTE, which holds B + SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outdated and no longer in use is long past its useful life.

clue.text: Flower, elegant in wreathes

indicators.note: wreathes means twists into coils, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elegant flower woven into garlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose.

clue.text: In lines, stray dogs

indicators.note: In puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: tiers are rows or lines
to err is to stray from what is right

explanation.surface: Stray dogs lined up in rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Terriers are a group of small, lively dog breeds.

clue.text: Riding a filly originally, ground beneath one

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
originally picks the opening letter of filly

explanation.surface: Riding a young mare first on the ground, beneath a rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges RIDINGA plus F from 'originally' filly. 'Infra dig' is short for Latin infra dignitatem.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infra dig is below one's dignity, unworthy of oneself.

clue.text: Instrument: piano appearing in unusual fresco

indicators.note: appearing in puts one piece inside another
unusual signals the letters of fresco in an odd arrangement

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A soft instrument shown in an unusual wall painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are a pincer-like surgical instrument.

clue.text: Down and dirty

definitions.meaning: smutty, risqué, as a coarse joke or film

explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means both melancholy and indecent.

clue.text: Loon perhaps guzzling last of cider — one for the road?

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the loon is the North American name for the bird Britons call a diver

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of cider

explanation.surface: A fool drinks up the rest of the cider and has one for the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loon' looks like a fool and 'one for the road' a last drink; it is a bird and a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is someone whose place is on the road.

clue.text: Conventional piece from bohemian or malcontent

indicators.note: piece from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something ordinary drawn from an unconventional or discontented person.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional and standard both describe what is usual and expected.

clue.text: Second appearance in Scottish tribe recently recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Highland clan recently made a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no signal; 'in' is that signal, and 'recalled' then reads the hidden run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebirth is a revival, coming into being once more.

clue.text: Floater, a large piece coming up

indicators.note: coming up in a down light means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a slab is a large thick piece

explanation.surface: A big piece of debris rising to the surface and floating.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood that floats readily.

clue.text: Before securing page he made errors in speech

indicators.note: securing means holding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: sooner means before, earlier

explanation.surface: Someone who blundered while speaking, before holding a page.
explanation.definitionFit: William Spooner, an Oxford don, gave his name to transposed initial sounds.

clue.text: Fabric in check, around which eleven buckles

indicators.note: around which says the jumbled letters enclose the check
buckles means bends out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to vet is to check

explanation.surface: A checked fabric around which eleven buckles are fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' looks like a tartan pattern on the fabric, but it is the verb meaning to examine.
explanation.definitionFit: Velveteen is a cotton cloth with a pile imitating velvet.

clue.text: State channel broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so we hear a word like another

parts.note: a main is a pipe or channel carrying water or gas

explanation.surface: A national TV channel being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: Joy drops hay all over the shop

indicators.note: all over the shop means in disarray, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A girl named Joy spills hay all over the store.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsody means ecstatic delight or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Tool competitors discussed in Australia?

indicators.note: discussed in Australia? marks a word spoken in an Australian accent, where the ay vowel sounds like eye

parts.note: players are competitors in a game

explanation.surface: Sports competitors being talked about Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a gripping hand tool with pincer jaws.
